First, we differentiate both sides of the equation with respect to $x,$ assuming that $y=y(x).$

Note that to differentiate the $x\operatorname{ln}⁡y$ term, we will need to use the product rule.

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}x\operatorname{ln}⁡(y) & =2x \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(x\operatorname{ln}⁡(y)) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2x) \\ [(x)(\frac{1}{y}\cdot \frac{\text{dy}}{\text{d}x})+(1)(\operatorname{ln}⁡(y))] & =2\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Now we solve the equation for $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\frac{x}{y}\left(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\right)+\operatorname{ln}⁡(y) & =2 \\ \frac{x}{y}\left(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\right) & =2-\operatorname{ln}⁡(y) \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{y(2-\operatorname{ln}⁡(y))}{x}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

First, we differentiate both sides of the equation with respect to $x,$ assuming that $y=y(x).$

Note that to differentiate the ${x}^{3}{e}^{y}$ term, we will need to use the product rule.

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}{x}^{3}{e}^{y} & =9{x}^{4} \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{3}{e}^{y}) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(9{x}^{4}) \\ [({x}^{3})({e}^{y}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x})+(3{x}^{2})({e}^{y})] & =36{x}^{3} \\ {x}^{3}\,{e}^{y}\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+3{x}^{2}{e}^{y} & =36{x}^{3}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Now we solve the equation for $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}{x}^{3}{e}^{y}\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+3{x}^{2}{e}^{y} & =36{x}^{3} \\ {x}^{3}{e}^{y}\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =36{x}^{3}-3{x}^{2}{e}^{y} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{36{x}^{3}-3{x}^{2}{e}^{y}}{{x}^{3}{e}^{y}} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{36}{{e}^{y}}-\frac{3}{x}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

First, we differentiate both sides of the equation with respect to $x,$ assuming that $y=y(x).$

 Note that to differentiate the ${x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡y$ term, we will need to use the product rule.

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(y)+4{y}^{4}=6{x}^{3} \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(y)+4{y}^{4}) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(6{x}^{3}) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(y))+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(4{y}^{4}) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(6{x}^{3}) \\ [{x}^{2}(-\operatorname{sin}⁡(y)\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x})+2x\operatorname{cos}⁡(y)]+16{y}^{3}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =18{x}^{2} \\ -{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(y)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+2x\operatorname{cos}⁡(y)+16{y}^{3}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =18{x}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Now we solve the equation for $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}-{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(y)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+16{y}^{3}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =18{x}^{2}-2x\operatorname{cos}⁡(y) \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}(16{y}^{3}-{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(y)) & =18{x}^{2}-2x\operatorname{cos}⁡(y) \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{18{x}^{2}-2x\operatorname{cos}⁡(y)}{16{y}^{3}-{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(y)}\end{aligned}
$$

Note that to differentiate the $7{x}^{3}{y}^{3}$ term, we will need to use the product rule.

$$
\begin{aligned}7{x}^{3}{y}^{3}+3{y}^{2} & =12{x}^{2} \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(7{x}^{3}{y}^{3}+3{y}^{2}) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(12{x}^{2}) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(7{x}^{3}{y}^{3})+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3{y}^{2}) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(12{x}^{2}) \\ [21{x}^{3}{y}^{2}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+21{x}^{2}{y}^{3}]+6y\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =24x \\ 21{x}^{3}{y}^{2}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+21{x}^{2}{y}^{3}+6y\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =24x\end{aligned}
$$

Now we solve the equation for $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}21{x}^{3}{y}^{2}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+6y\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =24x-21{x}^{2}{y}^{3} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}(21{x}^{3}{y}^{2}+6y) & =24x-21{x}^{2}{y}^{3} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{8x-7{x}^{2}{y}^{3}}{7{x}^{3}{y}^{2}+2y}\end{aligned}
$$

First, we differentiate both sides of the equation with respect to $x,$ assuming that $y=y(x).$

Note that to differentiate the $x\operatorname{sin}⁡y$ term, we will need to use the product rule.

$$
\begin{aligned}x\operatorname{sin}⁡(y)+{y}^{3}=2{x}^{3} \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(x\operatorname{sin}⁡(y)+{y}^{3}) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2{x}^{3}) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(x\operatorname{sin}⁡(y))+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({y}^{3}) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2{x}^{3}) \\ [x(\operatorname{cos}⁡(y)\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x})+\operatorname{sin}⁡(y)]+3{y}^{2}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =6{x}^{2} \\ x\operatorname{cos}⁡(y)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+\operatorname{sin}⁡(y)+3{y}^{2}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =6{x}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Now we solve the equation for $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x\operatorname{cos}⁡(y)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+3{y}^{2}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =6{x}^{2}-\operatorname{sin}⁡(y) \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}(x\operatorname{cos}⁡(y)+3{y}^{2}) & =6{x}^{2}-\operatorname{sin}⁡(y) \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{6{x}^{2}-\operatorname{sin}⁡(y)}{x\operatorname{cos}⁡(y)+3{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Note that to differentiate the $x{e}^{y}$ term, we will need to use the product rule.

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}x{e}^{y} & ={x}^{2} \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(x{e}^{y}) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{2}) \\ [(x)({e}^{y}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x})+(1)({e}^{y})] & =2x \\ x\,{e}^{y}\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+{e}^{y} & =2x\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Now we solve the equation for $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}x{e}^{y}\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+{e}^{y} & =2x \\ x{e}^{y}\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =2x-{e}^{y} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{2x-{e}^{y}}{x{e}^{y}}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

First, we differentiate both sides of the equation with respect to $x,$ assuming that $y=y(x).$

Note that to differentiate the ${x}^{2}y$ term, we will need to use the product rule.

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}y+4y & =2{x}^{3} \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{2}y+4y) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2{x}^{3}) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{2}y)+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(4y) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2{x}^{3}) \\ [{x}^{2}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+y\cdot 2x]+4\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =6{x}^{2} \\ {x}^{2}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+2xy+4\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =6{x}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Now we solve the equation for $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+4\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =6{x}^{2}-2xy \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}({x}^{2}+4) & =6{x}^{2}-2xy \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{6{x}^{2}-2xy}{{x}^{2}+4}\end{aligned}
$$

First, we differentiate both sides of the equation with respect to $x,$ assuming that $y=y(x).$

Note that to differentiate the $2xy$ term, we will need to use the product rule.

$$
\begin{aligned}2xy+4{y}^{3} & ={x}^{2}-1 \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2xy+4{y}^{3}) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{2}-1) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2xy)+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(4{y}^{3}) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{2}-1) \\ [2x\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+2y]+12{y}^{2}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =2x \\ 2x\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+2y+12{y}^{2}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =2x\end{aligned}
$$

Now we solve the equation for $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}2x\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+12{y}^{2}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =2x-2y \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}(2x+12{y}^{2}) & =2x-2y \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{2x-2y}{2x+12{y}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{x-y}{x+6{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

First, we differentiate both sides of the equation with respect to $x,$ assuming that $y=y(x).$

Note that to differentiate the $2{x}^{3}y$ term, we will need to use the product rule.

$$
\begin{aligned}2{x}^{3}y+2{y}^{2} & =4{x}^{2}+6 \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2{x}^{3}y+2{y}^{2}) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(4{x}^{2}+6) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2{x}^{3}y)+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2{y}^{2}) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(4{x}^{2}+6) \\ [2{x}^{3}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+y\cdot 6{x}^{2}]+4y\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =8x \\ 2{x}^{3}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+6{x}^{2}y+4y\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =8x\end{aligned}
$$

Now we solve the equation for $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}2{x}^{3}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+4y\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =8x-6{x}^{2}y \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}(2{x}^{3}+4y) & =8x-6{x}^{2}y \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{8x-6{x}^{2}y}{2{x}^{3}+4y}\end{aligned}
$$
